process_area.title: Executive Protection, Principal Travel & Event Security

value_stream.name: Corporate Security, Executive Protection & Travel Risk Management

fields.Participants: EP agents, principals' offices, drivers (W4683), GSOC (W4676)
fields.Trigger: Principal daily operations; threat-level change; event
fields.Volume: ~3–6 principals under routine EP (C-suite + family); details per principal

workflows.name: Executive Protection Program Design & Close-Protection Operations

Automation Opportunity: - EP scheduling/route-planning tools; protective-surveillance tech; drill-readiness tracker
Controls: - CTL-708 (ensure controlled execution — Executive Protection, Principal Travel & Event Security (PA-159.2).)
- CTL-708: EP posture matches threat profile (W4678); drills maintained; GSOC coordination
Cross-references: - links to W4676 (GSOC), W4678 (profile), W4683 (transport), W4686 (K&R response), VS-26 (K&R insurance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Complacency risk**: Routine EP that drills down to ceremony fails in a real incident; mitigated by realistic drills and posture review
- **Profile-too-high risk**: Overt EP attracting attention/creating target; mitigated by low-profile posture where appropriate
System Touchpoints: - EP scheduling/operations system; comms; GSOC (W4676); principal profile (W4678); records (VS-88)

steps.activity: Design and operate the EP program: standing close-protection details scaled to each principal's threat profile (W4678), protective logistics (vehicles, comms, medical), and the low-profile/high-profile posture toggle

Execute daily EP operations: principal movements, venue/vehicle advance, protective surveillance and counter-surveillance, access control at principal engagements; coordinate with GSOC (W4676) and route security (W4683)
Review EP posture after each significant movement/event; capture lessons and adjust; maintain EP readiness drills (medical, evacuation, attack response)

fields.Participants: EP agents (advance + traveling), Travel/Mobility (VS-160), intelligence (W4679), local fixers/security

Automation Opportunity: - Advance-checklist workflow; destination-risk feed; check-in/tracking automation
Controls: - CTL-708 (ensure controlled execution — Executive Protection, Principal Travel & Event Security (PA-159.2).)
- CTL-708: protective advance completed per trip; GSOC check-in maintained; post-trip debrief
Cross-references: - links to W4679 (destination risk), W4687/W4688 (travel tracking/lost-contact), VS-160 (mobility), W4686 (K&R)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Thin-advance risk**: Insufficient advance on an unfamiliar destination → exposure; mitigated by the advance checklist and local liaison
- **Lost-contact risk**: Principal out of contact in a high-risk destination; mitigated by GSOC check-in cadence and W4688 protocol

steps.activity: For each principal trip, conduct the protective advance: destination threat assessment (W4679), lodging/venue/transport vetting, route planning, medical/hospital identification, local security/law-enforcement liaison, and comms plan
Deploy traveling EP and coordinate with the principal's itinerary; maintain GSOC check-in cadence (W4676) and traveler-tracking (W4687); manage deviations and emerging threats
Conduct post-trip debrief; capture intelligence and lessons; adjust destination-risk (W4679) and future advance templates

fields.Participants: EP-trained drivers, EP agents, GSOC (W4676), fleet (VS-06)

Automation Opportunity: - Route-planning with threat overlays; vehicle telematics/comms; route-variation enforcement
Controls: - CTL-708 (ensure controlled execution — Executive Protection, Principal Travel & Event Security (PA-159.2).)
- CTL-708: vetted/trained drivers; route variation + counter-surveillance; executive fleet maintained
Cross-references: - distinct from VS-06 (goods fleet) and VS-141 (employee commute); links to W4676 (GSOC), W4681 (EP)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Predictable-route risk**: A predictable principal route enables premeditated attack; mitigated by route variation and counter-surveillance
- **Vehicle-failure risk**: Unmaintained/unarmored vehicle failing in a crisis; mitigated by dedicated executive-fleet maintenance
System Touchpoints: - Executive fleet (distinct from VS-06); route-planning; GSOC (W4676); vehicle comms/telematics
Time Estimate: - ~per movement absorbed in EP; fleet maintenance continuous

steps.activity: Operate the executive-transport program: EP-trained and vetted drivers, armored/reinforced vehicles where warranted, route planning (primary/alternate/evacuation), and convoy procedures for high-threat movements

Execute movements with route monitoring (GSOC W4676), counter-surveillance, and contingency (breakdown, ambush, roadblock) drills; coordinate with law enforcement for high-profile movements where appropriate
Maintain the executive fleet (acquisition, armoring, maintenance, comms) distinct from the goods fleet (VS-06) and employee commute (VS-141); vet and train drivers continuously

fields.Participants: EP (W4681), Marketing/Events (VS-14/VS-139), Facilities (VS-138), law enforcement, guard force (W4677)
fields.Trigger: Scheduled corporate event / AGM / high-profile public appearance (VS-36 board)
fields.Volume: ~15–25 high-profile events/year (AGM, board meetings, major launches, trade shows VS-139, community events)

workflows.name: Corporate Event, AGM & High-Profile Appearance Security

Automation Opportunity: - Event-security planning template; venue/access-control integration; crowd-monitoring tech
Controls: - CTL-708 (ensure controlled execution — Executive Protection, Principal Travel & Event Security (PA-159.2).)
- CTL-708: every high-profile event has a threat assessment + venue survey; crowd/civil-unrest readiness; post-event debrief
Cross-references: - links to W4674 (threat assessment), W4681 (EP), W4692 (civil-unrest), VS-14/VS-139 (events), VS-36 (board/AGM), VS-152 (community events)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-planned-event risk**: A high-profile appearance without a venue survey/threat assessment → exposure; mitigated by mandatory pre-event assessment
- **Crowd/protest risk**: Unmanaged protest/crowd at an event → reputational and safety harm; mitigated by crowd-management and W4692 readiness
System Touchpoints: - Event ops (VS-14/VS-139); access control/CCTV (W4677); GSOC (W4676); case management (W4696)

steps.activity: Conduct event threat assessment (W4674) and venue security survey (access control, screening, perimeters, exit routes, medical, comms); coordinate with marketing/events (VS-14/VS-139) and venue/facilities (VS-138)
Staff and operate event security (screening, crowd management, principal protection W4681, protest/civil-unrest readiness W4692); coordinate law-enforcement liaison for high-profile events
steps.r: Event Security Manager / Guard Force / EP

steps.activity: Debrief post-event; capture intelligence, incidents, and lessons; adjust future event-security templates

fields.Participants: EP (W4681), guard force (W4677), facilities/smart-home tech, principals' households
fields.Trigger: Principal residence setup; threat-level change; periodic review

workflows.name: Residences, Estate & Perimeter Security for Principals

Automation Opportunity: - Residential-security integration to GSOC; smart-home/perimeter tech; household-staff vetting workflow
Controls: - CTL-708 (ensure controlled execution — Executive Protection, Principal Travel & Event Security (PA-159.2).)
- CTL-708: residential security scaled to threat profile; location privacy (VS-91); household-staff vetting
Cross-references: - links to W4676 (GSOC), W4678 (profile), W4681 (EP), VS-91 (privacy), VS-161 (staff TPRM if outsourced)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Residence-exposure risk**: Residence location/schedule leaked → targeted home-invasion/kidnap; mitigated by location privacy (VS-91) and residential security
- **Insider-household risk**: A vetted-compromised household staff member; mitigated by household-staff vetting and confidentiality
System Touchpoints: - Residential alarm/CCTV/access; GSOC integration (W4676); smart-home tech; records (VS-88)

steps.activity: Design and install residential security: perimeter (fencing, lighting, sensors), access control, CCTV/panic-rooms, safe areas, comms, and guard posting scaled to the principal's threat profile (W4678)
Operate residential security: guard posting, alarm/CCTV monitoring (linked to GSOC W4676), household-staff vetting, and household-security briefings; manage privacy of residence location (VS-91)
Review residential security periodically and on threat change; coordinate with EP arrivals/departures (W4681/W4683) and residence-staff confidentiality

fields.Participants: CEO, VP Legal (VS-100.3), CFO, K&R insurer/consultant (VS-26), law enforcement (PNP/PNP-ACG/NBI), comms (VS-14.3), GSOC (W4676)

workflows.name: Kidnap & Ransom (K&R), Extortion & Blackmail Response Protocol

Automation Opportunity: - Crisis-response activation workflow; secure comms; tabletop-scheduling tracker
Controls: - CTL-708 (ensure controlled execution — Executive Protection, Principal Travel & Event Security (PA-159.2).)
- CTL-708: K&R protocol rehearsed; K&R insurer/consultant engaged (VS-26); information control; Legal-guided payment decisions
Cross-references: - links to VS-26 (K&R insurance/BCP), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-14.3 (crisis comms), VS-83 (victim/family support), W4676 (GSOC), W4694 (incident response)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unrehearsed-response risk**: A kidnap with no rehearsed protocol → catastrophic delay/error; mitigated by continuous rehearsal and K&R consultant pre-engagement (VS-26)
- **Information-leakage risk**: Leakage during an incident endangers the victim; mitigated by strict information control and limited need-to-know
- **Payment/legal risk**: Improper ransom/payment creating legal/ABC exposure; mitigated by Legal (VS-100.3) and insurer guidance
System Touchpoints: - Crisis-response protocol/case system; K&R insurance (VS-26); law-enforcement liaison; comms (VS-14.3); GSOC (W4676)

steps.activity: Maintain and rehearse the K&R/extortion response protocol: incident activation, crisis-response team, law-enforcement notification, K&R insurer/consultant engagement (VS-26), negotiator coordination, and family/principal liaison — with strict information control
steps.r: CSO / Crisis Response Lead / K&R Consultant

steps.activity: On incident: activate the protocol, engage law enforcement and K&R consultant, manage communications/information (avoid leakage that endangers the victim), and coordinate ransom/payment decisions per policy and law
steps.r: CSO / VP Legal / CFO / K&R Consultant

steps.activity: Conduct post-incident review (with the K&R consultant and law enforcement); capture lessons, support the victim/family recovery (VS-83), and adjust protocols and insurance (VS-26)

fields.Owner: Travel Risk Manager / CSO (joint with Travel/Mobility VS-160)
fields.Volume: ~300–500 tracked business trips/year (buyer/sourcing VS-122, executive, field-sales VS-140, audit VS-21, training)

workflows.name: Employee Travel Risk, Pre-Travel Briefing & Itinerary Tracking

Automation Opportunity: - Destination-risk screen at booking; itinerary-tracking platform; automated check-in and geo-alerting
Controls: - CTL-708 (ensure controlled execution — Executive Protection, Principal Travel & Event Security (PA-159.2).)
- CTL-708: elevated-risk trips briefed + tracked; duty-of-care documented; insurance confirmed
Cross-references: - distinct from VS-141 (daily commute); links to VS-160 (mobility), W4679 (destination risk), W4688 (lost-contact/medevac), VS-26 (insurance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Duty-of-care risk**: An employee harmed on a business trip to a known-risk destination without briefing/tracking → employer liability; mitigated by mandatory pre-travel briefing + tracking
- **Blind-traveler risk**: A traveler the GSOC cannot locate in a crisis; mitigated by itinerary-tracking and check-in cadence
System Touchpoints: - Travel booking (VS-160); itinerary-tracking platform; destination-risk (W4679); GSOC (W4676); insurance (VS-26)
Time Estimate: - ~per elevated-risk trip 0.5–1 day briefing + trip monitoring

steps.activity: For each business trip, screen the destination against travel-risk intelligence (W4679); require pre-travel briefing for elevated-risk destinations (threats, health, local laws, emergency contacts, check-in cadence)

Enroll the traveler in itinerary tracking (linked to GSOC W4676) for the trip duration; confirm travel/medical insurance and K&R coverage applicability (VS-26); brief duty-of-care obligations to the manager
Monitor active travelers for emerging destination threats (W4676); on threat, alert and advise (shelter, relocate, evacuate — W4688); debrief high-risk trips

fields.Owner: GSOC Manager / CSO (joint with HR/OH VS-83)
fields.Participants: HR (VS-19), Occupational Health (VS-83), medical-evac provider, insurance (VS-26), family, law enforcement/embassy
fields.Trigger: Traveler lost-contact, medical emergency, or destination crisis during a trip

workflows.name: Employee Travel Risk, Lost-Contact & Medical-Evacuation Coordination (Duty of Care)

Automation Opportunity: - Automated missed-check-in escalation; medevac-provider one-touch activation; family-liaison workflow
Controls: - CTL-708 (ensure controlled execution — Executive Protection, Principal Travel & Event Security (PA-159.2).)
- CTL-708: lost-contact thresholds + escalation; medevac provider pre-engaged; duty-of-care documentation
Cross-references: - links to W4687 (tracking), VS-83 (occupational health/recovery), VS-26 (insurance/medevac), VS-19 (HR/family)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Slow-escalation risk**: A missed check-in not escalated → delay in a real emergency; mitigated by clear thresholds and automated escalation
- **No-medevac-arrangement risk**: A medical emergency with no pre-arranged medevac → catastrophic delay; mitigated by pre-engaged provider and insurance (VS-26)

steps.activity: Maintain the lost-contact/medical-evacuation protocol: trigger thresholds (missed check-in, destination crisis, medical event), escalation, medical-evac provider engagement, and family liaison

On a lost-contact/medical event: activate the protocol, locate the traveler (tracking W4687), engage medical-evac and insurance (VS-26), support family, and coordinate with local authorities/embassy for international incidents
Conduct post-incident review; support the employee's return/recovery (VS-83); adjust travel-risk intelligence (W4679) and protocols
